title: Delay Relief Rate on Same-Day Confirmed Changes
content:
**Customer care note — Crestline Tickets by Fare Brand.** When the flight a same-day confirmed exchange moves away from was running late, the same-day change fee of that exchange is multiplied by the **delay relief rate**. The rate acts on the unrounded fee, and the fee is rounded to the cent only at the end.

## Which delay counts

The delay relief rate follows the longest arrival delay shown on a delay record of the segment being changed for the flight date of that exchange:

- *the exchange* is the latest same-day confirmed exchange recorded on the ticket, and its date is the flight date looked at;
- *the segment being changed* is the ticket's first unflown segment;
- only disruption records of type delay count, and the longest arrival delay in minutes among them is used.

## The rate

| Longest arrival delay on such a record | Delay relief rate |
|---|---|
| 120 minutes or more | 0 |
| At least 60 minutes and below 120 minutes | 0.45 |
| Below 60 minutes, or no delay record | 1 |

## Boundary cases (hypothetical)

| Longest delay | Rate |
|---|---|
| 120 minutes | 0 |
| 119 minutes | 0.45 |
| 60 minutes | 0.45 |
| 59 minutes | 1 |
| A delay record of 150 minutes whose flight date is the day before the exchange | Not counted; rate 1 if no other record qualifies |
| A delay record of 150 minutes on a different segment | Not counted |

*Worked figure (hypothetical).* A fee of 60 dollars with a delay relief rate of 0.45 becomes 27.00 dollars.
